findings.title: Dayjs objects compared with === never match, breaking 'unavailable' date overrides
findings.body: In checkIfIsAvailable the guard for a full-day block is `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes") === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, "minutes")`. Dayjs factory calls always return distinct object instances, so this strict equality is never true regardless of the underlying times. The intended 'start equals end means mark the whole day unavailable' case is therefore never detected: for a blocked day, a slot that spans the block timestamp falls through all the other conditions, find() returns undefined, dateOverrideExist is true, and the function returns true (available). Result: slots overlapping an 'unavailable' date override are still shown as bookable. Use .isSame() (or compare .valueOf()) instead.

findings.title: Working-hours check compares slot end minutes to slot start minutes
findings.body: In the newly added working-hours check inside checkIfIsAvailable, `const end = slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute();` is identical to `start` two lines above. Because of this, the condition `end > workingHour.endTime` can never be true, so slots that start inside working hours but whose end (start + eventLength) exceeds the end of the working hours are incorrectly reported as available. The `end` computation should include the event length, e.g. `start + eventLength`.

findings.title: Working-hours minutes compared in different timezones (organizer vs UTC)
findings.body: The new working-hours check computes `slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute()` from the slot's UTC time and compares it to `workingHour.startTime`/`endTime`. Per the WorkingHours type comment (packages/types/schedule.d.ts), those values are 'minutes since midnight; serialized to UTC by using the organizer timeZone'. So the comparison mixes organizer-local minutes with UTC minutes and is wrong whenever the organizer's timezone is not UTC: for example an organizer in IST with hours 09:30-18:00 local gets workingHour.startTime=570, but a 04:00 UTC slot (09:30 IST) yields 240 < 570 and is rejected, while a 12:00 UTC slot (17:30 IST) passes even though only 30 minutes of the day remain. The slot time must first be converted to the organizer timezone (organizerTimeZone is already passed in) before extracting hour/minute. Note this same mismatch affects the day-of-week check via slotStartTime.day().

findings.title: Date-override day match compares organizer-local date against UTC slot date
findings.body: In checkIfIsAvailable, the override's day is computed by converting `date.start` into the organizer's wall-clock time (`dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, 'minutes').format('YYYY MM DD')`) but it is compared against `slotStartTime.format('YYYY MM DD')`, which is the slot's UTC date. When the organizer's timezone is not UTC, the two dates only coincide by accident; for organizers east of UTC an override late in their local day maps to the next UTC day's slots and vice versa, so overrides apply to (or are skipped for) the wrong day. The slot date should be converted to the organizer timezone (e.g. dayjs.tz(slotStartTime, organizerTimeZone)) before the comparison.

findings.title: Override minute conversion drops day information and can produce inverted ranges
findings.body: The new offset conversion computes startTime/endTime as `dayjs(override.start).utc().add(offset, 'minute').hour() * 60 + .minute()`. Only the wall-clock hour/minute of the shifted instant is kept, so when the timezone offset shifts the override into the previous or next calendar day relative to the invitee day being computed, the resulting minute value silently wraps around midnight: an override whose shifted start is 23:30 yields startTime=1410 while endTime (shifted to 00:30 next day) yields 30, giving startTime > endTime. buildSlots then discards the range ('bypass invalid value' when start >= end), so the override disappears and the day falls back to nothing (the user's normal working hours for that day were already spliced out), leaving zero availability instead of the override window. The calculation should also adjust for the day shift (e.g. compare dates and add/subtract 24h of minutes).

findings.title: Override offset computed via Date.toString() parsed in server-local timezone
findings.body: `dayjs(override.start.toString()).tz(override.timeZone).utcOffset()` stringifies the Date in the server's local timezone and re-parses it with dayjs (also local), then converts to the organizer timezone. Because both the stringify and the parse use the same local zone the instant is approximately preserved, but this is fragile (toString includes a timezone name/offset that dayjs parsing may or may not honor consistently) and it is simpler and safer to use `dayjs(override.start).tz(override.timeZone).utcOffset()`. Additionally, `override.timeZone` is optional in the TimeRange type; if a caller omits it (e.g. dynamic-event paths or other consumers of getSlots), `dayjs(...).tz(undefined)` silently falls back to the server's local timezone, producing wrong offsets with no error. Consider making it required or defaulting explicitly.

findings.title: No test for the primary fix: round-robin date overrides of fixed hosts
findings.body: The PR's headline fix (#8207) is that date overrides of fixed hosts are respected for round-robin events, implemented via the new dateOverrides/workingHours logic in checkIfIsAvailable and the isFixed filtering in getSchedule. The only test added is the timezone-variation case for a personal event's date override. There is no test with a ROUND_ROBIN event containing a fixed host with a date override (the scenario described in the PR's own manual test plan), so a regression in the fixed-host filtering (e.g. the working-hours minutes bug above) would go undetected. Add a test mirroring the manual steps: round-robin event, one fixed host with an override, one round-robin host, assert only fixed-host-available slots are returned.
